name: Felix
title: Roman governor of Judea
summary: Antonius Felix was a Roman procurator (governor) over Judea from about 52 to 59 AD. He is known from the Bible for having kept the apostle Paul imprisoned in Caesarea for two years, and for hearing Paul preach about faith, righteousness, and the coming judgment. He left Paul in prison to please the Jews and in hope of receiving a bribe.

keyEvents.title: Paul is brought before Felix
keyEvents.description: After Paul was arrested in Jerusalem, he was sent to Caesarea to stand trial before governor Felix. The high priest Ananias and the lawyer Tertullus presented the charges against Paul.

keyEvents.title: Paul defends himself before Felix
keyEvents.description: Paul defended himself against the charges and claimed that he had done nothing wrong, but that he worshipped God according to the Way, which his opponents called a sect.

keyEvents.title: Felix postpones judgment
keyEvents.description: Felice, who was well acquainted with the Way, postponed the case and said he would decide it when commander Lysias came down.

keyEvents.title: Felice hears Paul speak about faith in Christ
keyEvents.description: Felice came together with his Jewish wife Drusilla and heard Paul speak about faith in Christ Jesus. When Paul spoke about righteousness, self-control, and the coming judgment, Felice was frightened and sent Paul away.

keyEvents.title: Felice hopes for bribes
keyEvents.description: Felice repeatedly sent for Paul and talked with him, but secretly hoped that Paul would offer him a bribe to be released.

keyEvents.title: Felice leaves Paul in prison
keyEvents.description: After two years, Felice was succeeded by Porcius Festus as governor. To please the Jews, Felice left Paul in prison.
